forces.title: Commercial banking value shifting from balance sheet to transactions
forces.description: A fundamental shift is occurring in commercial banking where value creation is moving away from traditional lending (balance sheet) towards transaction services such as cash management, corporate treasury, payments, and FX. Over 60% of UK commercial banking revenue already resides in these non-lending activities. This redefines competitive dynamics, requiring Investment & Corporate Banking firms to prioritize ownership of daily financial flows to retain customer relationships and capture value from transaction data and engagement.
forces.source_title: The decade to redefine UK banking

forces.title: Intensifying competition from digital-first challengers
forces.description: Competition in commercial banking is intensifying from neobanks, fintechs, and embedded finance platforms that are expanding beyond payments into broader financial services. Challengers like Monzo Business excel in service quality for small businesses, while international banks compete for large corporate relationships. This risks incumbents retaining only credit relationships while losing daily customer interaction and the valuable transaction data, which is critical for future revenue growth and cross-selling opportunities in Investment & Corporate Banking.
forces.source_title: The decade to redefine UK banking

forces.title: AI accelerating disintermediation and competitive pressure
forces.description: AI's rapid adoption significantly changes the speed and economics of banking competition. Agentic AI can remove historical frictions in comparing providers, switching products, and moving money, leading to potential disintermediation for Investment & Corporate Banking. For instance, tokenised treasury products allow treasurers to earn yield on idle cash directly. This forces banks to innovate rapidly, as the traditional grace period for technology adoption is closing, and those unable to keep pace risk losing valuable corporate deposits and relationships.
forces.source_title: The decade to redefine UK banking

forces.title: New opportunities in emerging global financial services corridors
forces.description: The realignment of global financial services trade, particularly the emergence of faster-growing corridors connected to Asia and the Middle East, presents new commercial opportunities for UK Investment & Corporate Banking. The UK's incremental diversification towards markets like China, Hong Kong, Singapore, and the GCC allows it to intermediate capital and provide specialist expertise. Leveraging global reach beyond traditional bilateral relationships will drive future growth, offering avenues for corporate lending, trade finance, and capital markets activities in these dynamic regions.
forces.source_title: Global financial services trade in transition

forces.title: Weakening insurability increases corporate lending risk and cost
forces.description: As physical climate risks intensify, the availability and affordability of insurance coverage are declining, leading to wider protection gaps. Lenders typically require adequate insurance as a condition of corporate lending. If insurance becomes unavailable or excessively expensive, Investment & Corporate Banking firms providing corporate loans may tighten credit standards, shorten loan tenors, require additional collateral, or increase interest rates to compensate for higher retained risk. In extreme cases, this could hinder the ability to lend at all, impacting debt markets.
forces.source_title: Mind the protection gap: The risk to capital markets and the resilience financing imperative

forces.title: Elevated corporate insolvencies pose credit risk for banks
forces.description: Elevated insolvency levels across Western Europe, with construction accounting for a significant share in the UK, pose a key credit risk for Investment & Corporate Banking's corporate lending portfolio. This increases the potential for loan losses and necessitates proactive credit risk management. Rising interest rates, which make refinancing and variable-rate debt materially more expensive, further exacerbate financial fragility for corporate clients, contributing to increased default risk and requiring banks to stress-test their rate exposures.
forces.source_title: Q3 UK economic outlook: Growth holds, inflation bites

forces.title: AI-enabled automation transforming corporate and investment banking workflows
forces.description: Agentic AI offers significant opportunities to automate and streamline complex, exception-heavy workflows in corporate and investment banking, such as onboarding, KYC checks, trade controls, collateral, settlement, and corporate actions. By redesigning entire end-to-end workflows with specialized AI agents, banks can compress corporate onboarding from weeks to days and reduce compliance effort by up to 50%. This improves operational efficiency, lowers cost-to-serve, and returns significant capacity to bankers, leading to a structural competitive advantage for early adopters.
forces.source_title: The decade to redefine UK banking

forces.title: Organizing coverage around growth sectors and trade corridors
forces.description: Investment & Corporate Banking firms can boost commercial opportunities by aligning relationship management and product coverage with key growth sectors (e.g., advanced manufacturing, clean energy, defence, life sciences) and active UK trade corridors. This sector and corridor expertise enables banks to proactively shape financing and transaction structures, bundling payments, letters of credit, guarantees, supply-chain finance, and hedging around clients' expansion needs. This approach allows for earlier engagement and deeper client relationships, fostering organic growth.
forces.source_title: The decade to redefine UK banking

forces.title: New financing models for climate adaptation and resilience
forces.description: The growing need for climate adaptation and resilience financing, estimated at £11bn annually in the UK, presents new opportunities for Investment & Corporate Banking. While adaptation projects often lack predictable revenues, there's increasing scope for 'balance-sheet solutions' like loans or bonds linked to resilience capital expenditure. Lenders can underwrite strengthened business continuity and reward enhanced borrower creditworthiness. Integrating adaptation financing into broader transactions, as exemplified by blended finance structures, also unlocks private capital and creates value-protection opportunities.
forces.source_title: Mind the protection gap: The risk to capital markets and the resilience financing imperative

forces.title: Regulatory fragmentation increases cross-border financial services costs
forces.description: Increasing regulatory fragmentation across international financial centres poses a significant risk to the UK's Investment & Corporate Banking sector. Such fragmentation can raise the cost of cross-border business, impacting the profitability and competitiveness of wholesale banking, trade finance, and other international intermediation functions. This challenges the UK's position as a global financial hub, potentially leading to activity migration closer to pools of capital and end-markets, requiring active nurturing of global relationships to mitigate threats.
forces.source_title: Global financial services trade in transition

forces.title: Winning mid-size business opportunities through tailored solutions
forces.description: Mid-size companies represent a distinct opportunity for Investment & Corporate Banking, requiring tailored solutions beyond scaled-up small-business banking or simplified large corporate coverage. Banks can serve these clients by combining cash forecasting, short-term liquidity investments, foreign exchange, trade finance, and working-capital support through digitally enabled service models. This focus allows relationship managers to deliver high-value advice and execution, strengthening client relationships and capturing a crucial segment of the corporate lending and transaction banking market.
forces.source_title: The decade to redefine UK banking

forces.title: Integration of climate risk into capital allocation decisions
forces.description: Climate risk projections are increasingly being incorporated into capital allocation decisions across financial markets, directing capital towards more resilient assets and away from significant risk exposure. This structural change impacts Investment & Corporate Banking by influencing demand for certain types of financing and advisory services. Banks need to integrate these considerations into their corporate lending and DCM/ECM strategies, leveraging public-private finance to de-risk adaptation and resilience investments, which can improve risk-adjusted returns and attract private capital.
forces.source_title: Mind the protection gap: The risk to capital markets and the resilience financing imperative

forces.title: AI enhancing productivity in relationship management for corporate clients
forces.description: The application of AI to rewired workflows in frontline relationship management teams serving corporate clients is showing significant productivity gains. By shifting certain tasks to AI agents, banks have observed a 20-40% lower cost to serve and 10-12 hours per week of capacity returned to each banker. This allows relationship managers to focus on higher-value advisory and execution for corporate clients, improving service quality and efficiency in areas like corporate lending, trade finance, and transaction banking, thereby boosting overall CIB strategy effectiveness.
forces.source_title: The decade to redefine UK banking

forces.title: Higher interest rates increase corporate borrowing costs
forces.description: The Bank of England's expected rate hike to 4.00% in September 2026, combined with Gilt yields at 4.80%, makes refinancing and variable-rate corporate debt materially more expensive. This directly impacts corporate clients' financial flexibility and their demand for new corporate lending. Investment & Corporate Banking firms will face challenges in maintaining lending volumes and may see increased pressure on existing loan portfolios as corporate clients contend with higher debt servicing costs and potentially reduced investment capacity due to economic uncertainty.
forces.source_title: Q3 UK economic outlook: Growth holds, inflation bites

forces.title: Improving recognition of resilience measures in financing terms
forces.description: A growing trend towards improved recognition of verified resilience measures in the pricing and terms of financing presents an upside for Investment & Corporate Banking. This could include premium credits, deductible reductions, coverage enhancements, or longer loan tenors for corporate clients that demonstrate material risk reduction through adaptation investments. Such mechanisms incentivize proactive risk management, making assets more 'bankable' and 'investable.' This helps banks in corporate lending and DCM activities to differentiate offerings and mitigate climate-related credit risks.
forces.source_title: Mind the protection gap: The risk to capital markets and the resilience financing imperative

viewpoints.title: UK financial services must capitalize on diversification into emerging markets
viewpoints.description: The UK's financial services exports, though concentrated in advanced economies like the EU and US, show increasing diversification into fast-growing emerging markets, particularly across Asia and the Middle East. This presents significant opportunities for the UK to leverage its capabilities in capital markets, international banking, and specialist expertise to intermediate capital and build complementary relationships with regional hubs. Understanding and servicing these realigning global trade corridors will be crucial for future commercial success and to enhance economic resilience.
viewpoints.source_title: Global financial services trade in transition

viewpoints.title: UK banking's profitability masks strategic vulnerability from new competition
viewpoints.description: Despite current high profitability, the UK banking sector, including commercial banking, faces rapid erosion of its foundations due to shifting customer primacy, intense competition, and accelerating AI adoption. Over 60% of UK commercial-banking revenue already lies outside lending, with value moving to the transaction layer. Neobanks and fintechs capture a significant share of relationships, and AI will further accelerate disintermediation by making it easier for customers to switch providers and manage money. Banks must act with precision and speed to secure customer primacy and rebuild their cost base.
viewpoints.source_title: The decade to redefine UK banking

viewpoints.title: AI's rapid adoption accelerates competitive pressure for UK banks
viewpoints.description: AI adoption is occurring far faster and more broadly than previous technologies, closing the grace period for incumbent banks. This accelerates disintermediation by removing friction in processes like comparing rates, switching accounts, and moving money. If left unaddressed, deposit profits could fall by 20% or more, potentially shrinking global bank profit pools by $170 billion over the next decade. UK banks must quickly leverage AI as their sharpest tool by becoming a trusted AI interface for customers, combining their advantages in data, regulation, and scale.
viewpoints.source_title: The decade to redefine UK banking

viewpoints.title: Incumbents can leverage trust to lead in AI-powered financial services
viewpoints.description: While AI presents significant disintermediation threats, incumbent banks retain a crucial advantage: trust. 64% of UK AI users trust their primary bank most for AI services, compared to 16% for major tech companies. This trust creates an opening for banks to turn AI into a strategic asset, provided they move quickly. Banks with large tech budgets, proprietary data, established relationships, and regulatory experience are well-positioned to build trusted AI interfaces and leverage AI to transform operations and customer engagement, securing their competitive position.
viewpoints.source_title: The decade to redefine UK banking

viewpoints.title: Climate change poses systemic financial risk through insurability decline
viewpoints.description: Climate change is evolving into a financial stability issue, not just a physical risk. As climate hazards intensify, rising insured losses will tighten insurance markets, widening the protection gap. This, in turn, reduces bankability and investability across the real economy, as lending and investment activities rely on adequate insurance. This systemic risk transmission channel may materialise quicker than wider economic impacts, requiring focused attention and coordinated action across public and private sectors to strengthen insurability and support resilience investment.
viewpoints.source_title: Mind the protection gap: The risk to capital markets and the resilience financing imperative

viewpoints.title: Adaptation and resilience are critical core economic infrastructure investments
viewpoints.description: Underinvestment in climate adaptation and resilience risks reinforcing a negative loop where rising losses weaken insurability, discourage private investment, and strain public finances. Adaptation and resilience measures should be considered core economic infrastructure, essential for preserving insurability, protecting asset values, and ensuring the effective functioning of capital markets. Significant capital mobilisation is required to meet domestic and global adaptation and resilience needs, presenting both a risk and an opportunity for the UK's financial markets to play an important role.
viewpoints.source_title: Mind the protection gap: The risk to capital markets and the resilience financing imperative
